name: Edie Sedgwick
label: Dischord
lede: El Guapo's bass player put on a dress, became Andy Warhol's most famous Superstar, and sang songs named after Angelina Jolie, Rob Lowe and Ol' Dirty Bastard, some of them produced by Ian MacKaye.

eras.title: Two Sedgwicks and a list of movie stars
eras.text: It started as a duo: Justin Moyer of El Guapo on bass and vocals, Ryan Hicks on drums, both taking the surname Sedgwick. Every song was named for a celebrity, and the whole thing stopped almost as soon as the first record was out.

years.h: Justin Moyer and Ryan Hicks start Edie Sedgwick
years.p: [[Justin Moyer|68cb15fd-5c0c-4b60-ad06-935ac0756a4d]], still in El Guapo, starts Edie Sedgwick as a two-piece with drummer [[Ryan Hicks|82e2e1d5-cc55-47a3-8ffe-1c10c30401fa]], both billed with the surname Sedgwick. The real Edie Sedgwick, Andy Warhol's Superstar, died of a barbiturate overdose in 1971, as Dischord's bio notes.

q: This is the weirdest album I've ever made.
Justin Moyer, to the New York Times
years.p: Edie Sedgwick's debut: thirteen minimal songs, each titled for a star: "Faye Dunaway," "Winona Ryder," "Tom Cruise," "Meryl Streep," and last of all "Edie Sedgwick." Released by Mud Memory together with Dischord.
years.xp:
Dischord's page documents it as the original two-piece: Justin Moyer on bass and vocals, Ryan Hicks on drums. The celebrity-title format would stick for the next decade.

Dischord quotes Moyer telling the New York Times it was the strangest thing he'd made, which, coming from a member of El Guapo, is saying something.

years.h: Justin Moyer's epilepsy diagnosis puts Edie Sedgwick on hiatus
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Justin Moyer was diagnosed with epilepsy in 2001, and his duo with Ryan Hicks went on hiatus.

eras.title: A dress, a wig and an iPod
eras.text: When Edie Sedgwick came back in 2004, it was Justin Moyer alone, performing in drag, singing over backing tracks on an iPod, right as electroclash was peaking and celebrity culture was going fully tabloid.

years.h: Justin Moyer returns as Edie Sedgwick, solo and in drag
years.p: Dischord's bio: in 2004 Justin Moyer began performing solo in drag as Edie Sedgwick, the reincarnation of the Warhol Superstar. Wikipedia describes it as a solo electroclash act backed by an iPod.
years.xp:
The act worked on two levels at once, auditory and visual, as Dischord puts it. The songs kept their celebrity names, and the show turned Moyer into a celebrity character singing about other celebrities, with Paris Hilton and Angelina Jolie among the references.

Dischord's bio frames it as an aesthetic that anticipated a 21st-century culture of fame, a few years before reality TV and social media made that obvious.

years.h: Edie Sedgwick's Her Love Is Real... But She Is Not
years.p: The first record of Justin Moyer's solo drag era as Edie Sedgwick, which Dischord carries in distribution.

eras.title: The band gets bigger, the dress comes off
eras.text: Ian MacKaye produced Edie Sedgwick's third album, and Justin Moyer rebuilt the act as a live band with an all-female backing line-up. Four years and four Dischord releases later, the project was called E.D. Sedgwick and the dress was gone.

years.cap: Things Are Getting Sinister And Sinisterer, Dischord No. 161, on translucent orange vinyl
years.h: Things Are Getting Sinister And Sinisterer · Dischord No. 161
years.p: Edie Sedgwick's third album, produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and Justin Moyer at Studio 1654. Songs include "Sissy Spacek," "Angelina Jolie," "Rob Lowe," "ODB" and "Bambi_G.W. Bush."

years.h: Edie Sedgwick becomes a band with an all-female line-up
years.p: Wikipedia dates it to 2008: Justin Moyer out front, with Kristina Buddenhagen on bass, Jess Matthews on drums, Carla Elliot on vocals, and [[Basla Andolsun|ca1ce6ba-8758-49b2-b2b0-573e80659fb2]], later of [[Andalusians|a7572df1-aad3-4851-ab0c-6013a5dbbb6d]], among the players.

years.h: Live at the Black Cat, March 29, 2009
yt: Live at the Black Cat, March 29, 2009

years.h: Love Gets Lovelier Every Day · Dischord No. 169
years.p: Edie Sedgwick's limited three-song 7-inch comes with a download of all eleven tracks, including a mix of Van Halen's "Everybody Wants Some" and a song called "Ava Devine."

years.h: Edie Sedgwick's Heat Wave, remixed by [[Greg Saunier|2ae4e9b4-9e8b-4a98-920d-4f3a881dac96]] and others
years.p: Edie Sedgwick's single "Heat Wave" comes out via Mud Memory and Dischord, then as a white-label 12-inch (Dischord No. 175.5) with remixes by Deerhoof's Saunier, Triobelisk (Shelby Cinca of [[Frodus|ea524f94-2e37-414d-a7e9-61ba96472f0a]]) and Philadelphia's Pink Skull.

years.h: Justin Moyer writes a SXSW tour diary for City Paper
years.p: Washington City Paper runs Justin Moyer's "Heat Wave: Edie Sedgwick Goes to SXSW" day by day. Moyer, almost 35, sleeps on a Cleveland floor with a drum throne for a pillow.

years.h: We Wear White, as E.D. Sedgwick · Dischord No. 175
years.p: Edie Sedgwick's fifth full-length comes out credited to E.D. Sedgwick, recorded mostly at Inner Ear and mixed by [[Phil Manley|726b1239-9ca1-4239-b0a0-2d64d0ec6683]]. Mother Jones's headline said Justin Moyer was sick of wearing a dress all the time.
years.xp:
Eleven songs, from "Hex of Sex (For Minimal Man)" to "Weatherman." JosaFeen Wells joins on vocals, with Kristina Buddenhagen and Jess Matthews still the rhythm section.

Phil Manley of [[Trans Am|7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338]] had also recorded Moyer's other band [[Antelope|bad5bc3a-a2e8-41d7-95aa-b5734784fbb1]] a decade earlier. The initials kept the name and dropped the costume.

eras.title: On hiatus, threatening to return
eras.text: Dischord says Edie Sedgwick is on extended hiatus but could emerge at any time. Meanwhile Justin Moyer kept making music under other names and built a second career at the Washington Post.

years.p: Justin Moyer's new project Light Beams, with Arthur Noll on bass and Sam Lavine on drums. Wikipedia notes its 2020 album Self Help won a Washington Area Music Association award.

years.h: Justin Moyer shares a Pulitzer at the Washington Post
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Justin Moyer was part of the Washington Post team whose coverage of the January 6 Capitol insurrection won a Pulitzer Prize.
